requirements.requirement: Deliver a copy of node1<->node2 traffic to node3 so a capture on node3 shows packets addressed to node1/node2 even though not destined for node3
requirements.summary: iptables mangle TEE rules on node1 (PREROUTING src=node2, OUTPUT dst=node2, gateway=node3) cloned traffic to node3 while preserving original addressing. Baseline first showed node3 saw nothing (switched segment), then after TEE rules node3's tcpdump on eth0 captured both ICMP echo request and reply packets addressed to 10.100.28.10/10.100.28.11 (not to node3), with TEE rule counters incrementing in step with the 4 pings sent.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between node1 and node2 keeps flowing as it did before mirroring is added
requirements.summary: Ping tests between node1 and node2 before mirroring, immediately after installing TEE rules, and after every subsequent node restart all showed 0% packet loss with normal latency, indicating the original path was never disrupted by the mirroring mechanism.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (8e8823ec...) and active mirror-service/TEE-rule state captured; reboot scheduled and acknowledged; several probes hit connection resets consistent with mid-reboot; boot_id confirmed changed to 5af44431... post-restart (matching the fixed after_executor snapshot); systemd service and TEE rules were auto-restored and a fresh ping+tcpdump round-trip proved mirroring worked again.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (c2ffc729...) captured; reboot scheduled; boot_id confirmed changed to 453a66a3... post-restart (matches fixed after_executor snapshot); eth0 addressing restored; subsequent ping+tcpdump test showed node1<->node2 traffic still flowing and still mirrored to node3.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (a0d04bc6...) captured; reboot scheduled; boot_id confirmed changed to 1b38f7c8... post-restart (matches fixed after_executor snapshot); eth0 addressing restored; final end-to-end test after all three nodes had cycled showed node1<->node2 ping at 0% loss with node3's tcpdump capturing the mirrored ICMP traffic.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence. Traffic mirroring was implemented on node1 via iptables mangle TEE rules that clone node1<->node2 traffic to node3 while preserving original addressing; node3's tcpdump captured the mirrored ICMP packets addressed to 10.100.28.10/.11 (not to node3), and TEE counters matched the number of pings sent. The original node1<->node2 path showed 0% packet loss throughout setup and after every subsequent restart. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was completed cleanly on all three nodes: each node has a pre-restart boot identity/healthy-state capture, a restart acknowledgement, a confirmed changed post-restart boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed before_prepare/after_executor snapshots), and a functional re-verification of mirroring afterward. Operational hygiene is good but not perfect: an initial tc/mirred+gretap mirroring attempt was tried, failed to deliver frames on the wire, and was fully cleaned up before the iptables TEE approach was adopted — a bounded, reverted troubleshooting mutation rather than residue.
limitations: Only ICMP traffic was used to validate mirroring end-to-end; the task's broader phrase 'traffic node1 exchanges with node2' is not explicitly tested with other protocols (TCP/UDP), though the iptables TEE rules match on IP address rather than protocol, so this is a minor evidence-coverage gap rather than a functional gap.
Restart evidence relies on ping+tcpdump snapshots taken shortly after each reboot; no extended soak period was captured, though this is consistent with a bounded verification window.

operational_hygiene.summary: The final solution (iptables mangle TEE rules + a systemd oneshot unit/modules-load entry for persistence) is minimal, directly tied to the task outcome, and left only expected residue (the new service/config files, which are required for the mirroring to persist). Before reaching that solution, the executor ran a bounded troubleshooting experiment using tc clsact/act_mirred plus gretap ('span0') tunnels and manual point-to-point IP addressing (172.30.0.1/30, 172.30.0.2/30) on node1 and node3, which never delivered mirrored frames onto the wire. This experiment mutated managed-node state (new tunnel interfaces, tc qdiscs/filters, temporary IP addresses) with no causal contribution to the final outcome, so it counts as an unnecessary mutation, but it was low-risk, fully reverted (tc filters/qdisc, span0 interfaces, and temporary addresses were explicitly removed via cmd-5df8414e1b274710, cmd-92170cd63c214199, cmd-f8c7455289a549a6) and left no residue in the final after_executor snapshot. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were introduced by the executor; the one new failed-service line seen on node2 post-restart (NetworkManager-wait-online.service) is a restart artifact unrelated to executor actions.
